summary: In this talk, Brian Balfour speaks directly to AI Product Managers who are feeling overwhelmed by the pace of industry developments. He asks the audience to reflect on the past 45 days and the flood of product launches, but immediately asserts that none of those launches matter unless one critical question is answered: what do I build and why will it win. Balfour's central thesis is that competitive advantage in AI products does not derive from the AI technology itself, which is increasingly commoditized and accessible. Instead, lasting advantage comes from three things that are uniquely yours: your proprietary data, your functionality, and your deep understanding of unmet customer needs. He recaps the framework by posing three sequential questions that AI PMs must answer. First, what are the unmet customer problems? This is a foundational product management principle that predates the AI wave. Second, what AI capabilities can solve those problems in novel ways? This is where AI enters the picture, not as the starting point but as a tool applied to well-understood problems. Third, what proprietary data can power those solutions? Data is positioned as a key differentiator that competitors cannot easily replicate. Balfour's overarching message is that AI PMs should not lead with the technology but with customer understanding and proprietary assets. The talk appears to be the opening portion of a longer presentation, as he promises to offer ideas and solutions to relieve audience stress by the end. This section establishes the strategic framework before likely diving into tactical guidance.
